sourceRefs.locator: Egerton MS 2817, one item, 1453. The catalogue describes the Greek text, the sultan’s monogram and the Arabic-script date and vizier’s signature.

Opening section, translation from the Paris Ottoman Turkish text, envoys with the keys, property and enslaved people, annual tax, bells, new churches and customs. Discussion of Lomellino’s letter and flight by sea at notes 26–30. Reprinted in Essays in Ottoman History, pp. 275–376.
Tarih İncelemeleri Dergisi 36/2, pp. 601–604, especially notes 59–65. Compares Lomellino, Doukas and Barbaro, describes taxation and names Greek, Italian and Ottoman witnesses to the grant.

MA thesis, pp. 41–43 on the envoys, pp. 113–118 on the scope, dating and omissions of the survey. Sections 3.6.1–2, pp. 123–125, record Marya Maryana’s houses and oven, the brothers de Franchi, Fabyan and Anton di Laştergo. Note 760 identifies the Genoese notarial act for the smith.

Museum location and map for the watchtower of medieval Pera (approximately 41.02565 N, 28.97413 E). The tower is a landmark for the historic district on the north shore. The places where the charter was delivered, the letter written and individual households stood are not identified.

Letter of Angelo Giovanni Lomellino from Pera to his brother, 23 June 1453, pp. 131–135. His nephew Imperiali and the defence of Constantinople, escape by sea, envoys at the sultan’s camp, advice to the doge and the refusal of ransom.

Prima serie di documenti riguardanti la colonia di Pera, Atti della Società Ligure di Storia Patria XIII, doc. CXLIX, pp. 229–233. The dateline names Pera, 23 June 1453. Ships depart on p. 230, the nephew appears on p. 232.

Galata survey, preamble and quarters Zani Drapora and Zani Dabdan, pp. 217–222. The register survives in fragments. The preamble specifies poll-tax liability, property confiscated for the treasury and rent. See Somer, pp. 114, 123–125, for the text and named entries.
